cards.text: Last time, David got his family back from the Amalekites. Meanwhile, the Philistines are at war with Israel, and Saul, Israel's king, is in the thick of it. Fair warning, friend: this one's heavy, so the jokes are taking a little break.

cards.question: The battle is on Mount Gilboa. How does it go for the men of Israel?

cards.text: The Philistines chase Saul and his sons hard. One of those sons is Jonathan, David's dear friend (1 Samuel 18:1-3).

cards.question: Jonathan, Saul's son, makes it out of the battle alive.

cards.text: Then the battle closes in on Saul himself. It gets fierce, fast.

cards.question: As the battle gets fierce around Saul, the ___ overtake him and wound him critically.

cards.text: Saul is badly wounded. He turns to his armor-bearer, because he doesn't want the Philistines getting to him first.

cards.question: What does wounded Saul ask his armor-bearer to do?

answers.text: Run him through with his sword

cards.question: Saul's armor-bearer does what Saul asks him to do.

cards.text: His armor-bearer is terrified and won't do it. So Saul takes his own sword and falls on it.

cards.question: When Saul's armor-bearer sees that Saul is dead, what does he do?

answers.text: Falls on his own sword too

cards.text: That same day, Saul, his three sons, his armor-bearer and all his men die together. And other Israelites are watching.

cards.question: The Israelites in the valley and across the Jordan see that the army fled and Saul and his sons are dead. What do they do?

answers.text: Crown a new king right away

cards.question: So the ___ came and moved into the cities those Israelites left behind.

cards.text: The next day, the Philistines come back to strip the dead. And there on Mount Gilboa, they find Saul and his three sons.

cards.question: The Philistines cut off Saul's ___ and strip off his ___.
The Philistines send messengers all over their land to spread the news about Saul. Where do the messengers announce it?

answers.text: In the temples of their idols
In the tents of Israel's army

cards.text: They put Saul's armor in the temple of the Ashtoreths. Then they hang his body up for everyone to see.

cards.question: The Philistines hang Saul's body on the wall of ___.

cards.text: Word reaches Jabesh-gilead, a town east of the Jordan. Years ago, Saul rescued that town from the Ammonites (1 Samuel 11:1-11).

cards.question: When the men of valor of Jabesh-gilead hear what the Philistines did to Saul, what do they do?

answers.text: Travel all night and bring the bodies back
Send word to David in Ziklag
Gather an army to attack Gath

cards.text: All night, friend. I can't make it past the second oven timer without nodding off. They bring Saul and his sons home to Jabesh and burn the bodies there.

cards.question: The men of Jabesh bury the bones under the ___ tree in Jabesh.
After the burial, the people of Jabesh fast for seven days.

findings.problem: The card says David got his family back from the Amalekites. That is a Bible fact from 1 Samuel 30, but no reference is given.

rule.text: **References.** Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: "Meanwhile" says the battle happens at the same time as David's rescue in chapter 30. 1 Samuel 31:1 opens with "Now" and does not say how the two events connect in time.

rule.text: **Leave open what the text leaves open:** who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: "Fair warning, friend: this one's heavy" tells the baker the battle goes badly before card 2 asks how it goes. That rules out "They hold the mountain" and "They drive the Philistines back."

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Papa Dorin tells the baker that "the jokes are taking a little break." Stop 2 card 8 then makes a joke anyway. The docs say his personality fits a tense moment, but they don't say whether he should announce dropping humor, or how much humor a passage about death and mutilation should carry.
findings.question: In a tragic passage, may Papa Dorin tell the baker he's setting the jokes aside? If he does, should the rest of the passage stay joke-free?

findings.problem: Most of the story cards in stop 1 are flat retelling with almost none of Papa Dorin's voice. Examples are card 5 ("Then the battle closes in on Saul himself. It gets fierce, fast."), card 10 and card 12.

rule.text: **Short, but not stripped down.** A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: "It gets fierce, fast" adds speed. 1 Samuel 31:3 only says the battle intensified against Saul.

rule.text: **Don't stretch the text.** Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: "for everyone to see" gives a purpose for hanging Saul's body. 1 Samuel 31:10 doesn't state one.

rule.text: **Reasons:** He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.

findings.problem: "a town east of the Jordan" is a fact from outside the passage. It has no reference. The only reference given is for Saul's rescue of the town.

rule.text: **References.** Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: "They bring Saul and his sons home to Jabesh" calls Jabesh Saul's home. 1 Samuel 31:12 only says "When they arrived at Jabesh," and Saul's home was not Jabesh.

rule.text: **Call things what the text calls them.**
